standard_prerequisites: The situation and the complex K produced in the existence argument, and the canonical map from K to the truncations of the module under consideration
Relative pseudo-coherence and the representation of the derived pushforward over an affine etale neighbourhood by a bounded above complex of finite free modules over a smooth presentation

The comparison of the cohomology of that complex after base change to the truncation with the corresponding modules, and the behaviour of ranks of maps of finite free modules under principal localisation
core_obligations: Fix a truncation index and interpret the third part of the statement through the canonical map from the complex to that truncation
Since the closed subset in question is quasi-compact, reduce to producing an open neighbourhood for one point of it, and further to an affine etale neighbourhood of that point

Choose a smooth presentation of the affine chart and represent the derived pushforward by a bounded above complex of finite free modules over that presentation, so that after base change to the truncation the cohomology is concentrated in degree zero and computed by the corresponding module

If the highest nonvanishing index of the complex is at most zero, all three properties hold; otherwise the connecting map at the top has maximal rank at the point, so after a principal localisation it becomes surjective and a splitting removes the top term
Conclude by induction on the highest nonvanishing index, which produces the required neighbourhood, and then cover the quasi-compact closed subset by finitely many such neighbourhoods
proof_roadmap: Reduce to a point and to an affine etale neighbourhood with a smooth presentation
Replace the complex by a bounded above complex of finite free modules and compute its cohomology after base change
Trim the top term by a maximal rank argument and principal localisation, inducting on the highest index
Cover the quasi-compact closed subset by the resulting neighbourhoods
difficulty_reason: The counted conclusion is the existence of an open neighbourhood of the closed subscheme on which the complex has a single cohomology sheaf, of finite presentation and computing the truncations, at source lines 2507-2521, label lemma-finitely-presented, whose proof occupies source lines 2523-2570. The proof is a genuinely local argument rather than a citation: it reduces to one point and to an affine etale neighbourhood, replaces the derived object by a bounded above complex of finite free modules over a smooth presentation using relative pseudo-coherence, and then runs an induction that trims the top term of the complex. The trimming needs a maximal rank observation at the point together with a principal localisation to make the connecting map surjective, after which a splitting removes the top term; the quasi-compactness of the closed subset then assembles the local neighbourhoods. The counted statement records neither the complex replacement nor the trimming induction.
